mainText: This is Dose of Good for Saturday, November 21. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Backyard bug hunt finds a rare ant scientists sought for 50 years. During Bugs in my Backyard week, Australians logged almost 30,000 insect sightings. Finds include the critically endangered dinosaur ant, photographed in South Australia, and the only known live photo of a rare beetle. Second: Public school in Rio's Maré favela wins a World's Best School Prize. GET IV Centenário was one of five global winners, in the overcoming-adversity category. Pupils get 20 minutes each morning to talk about their feelings and use robotics and 3D printing to solve local problems. Third: MIT's flying microrobot lands on a flower using its own sensors. Lighter than a paperclip, the four-winged robot followed a path and landed on a sunflower without lab cameras. Future versions could help with pollination and crop monitoring. Fourth: Potiguara Indigenous farmers bring in their first agroecological cotton harvest. In Paraíba, Brazil, families in the Potiguara Indigenous Territory harvested cotton grown alongside peanuts and beans, with no chemicals. The Embrapa-backed project trained growers, the association bought a tractor, and plots will expand next season. Fifth: Argentine scientists name a new beetle after rock musician Indio Solari. Bothynus indiosolari, a 15–20 mm rhinoceros beetle, was found in Chaco and Misiones. The name honours the Argentine musician, who died in June. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
